overview: The September 9-10 window brought 32 patches across 5 series to bpf-next. The headline work is a 15-patch v3 series from Justin Suess that introduces a BPF interface for applying Landlock security rulesets, adding new LSM policy object kfuncs and a hook for enforcing policies at exec time. Yonghong Song's 12-patch v2 series adds support for passing structs by value and __int128 arguments to kfuncs, aligning the calling convention with standard C ABI on both x86-64 and arm64.

patches.title: lsm: Add the LSM policy object lifetime hooks
patches.author: Justin Suess
patches.summary: This is the opening patch of a 15-patch v3 series titled "BPF interface for applying Landlock rulesets". The series adds a new LSM policy object abstraction with a full set of kfuncs (bpf_lsm_policy_from_fd, bpf_lsm_policy_acquire, bpf_lsm_policy_release, bpf_lsm_policy_apply_bprm) that let BPF programs acquire and apply Landlock rulesets to processes at exec time. A new bprm_apply_policy_object LSM hook fires during bprm setup, and Landlock's reference counting is updated to free rulesets safely after an RCU grace period. Comprehensive selftests and documentation are included.

patches.title: bpf: Support by-value struct arguments up to 16 bytes
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: This is one of the core patches in a 12-patch v2 series that extends kfunc argument passing to support structs passed by value (up to 16 bytes) and __int128. Previously all aggregate kfunc arguments had to be passed by pointer; this change introduces an ABI description layer that the JIT consults when laying out call arguments, and updates both the x86-64 and arm64 backends to follow standard calling conventions for small structs. The verifier gains the ability to recognise and validate these new argument kinds, and an extensive set of C and inline-assembly selftests covers all cases.

patches.title: bpf, x86: Use global buffer for trampoline size generation
patches.author: Jiri Olsa
patches.summary: This single patch (v2) changes the x86 BPF trampoline JIT to use a pre-allocated global buffer when calculating the trampoline size, rather than allocating memory just for the dry-run measurement pass. Allocating and immediately freeing memory solely to count bytes is wasteful and can fail under memory pressure, so switching to a static scratch buffer makes size estimation cheaper and more reliable. The actual trampoline image is still allocated normally once the correct size is known.

patches.title: bpf: Avoid soft lockup in __htab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch()
patches.author: Josef Bacik
patches.summary: This single patch (v2) adds a cond_resched() call inside the batch delete loop of the hash-table map implementation. When iterating over a very large hash table to delete entries, the kernel held the CPU continuously for the entire operation, which could trigger the soft lockup watchdog on busy systems. Inserting a reschedule point allows other tasks to run during long batch operations without changing the correctness of the deletion logic.

patches.title: bpftool: Skip non-autoload programs when generating light skeletons
patches.author: Thiébaud Weksteen
patches.summary: This 3-patch v2 series fixes bpftool's light skeleton (lskel) code generation when an object file contains programs marked as non-autoload. The generator was previously including such programs in the context size calculation and in the generated struct, producing invalid FDs and incorrectly sized contexts at runtime. The fix skips non-autoload programs during lskel generation, recomputes ctx.sz without relying on link counts, and adds selftests that verify the program FD is correct after non-autoload programs appear in the object.
